tasks.title: MutationOutcome gains None at zero, and ToResult rejects it
acceptance: A1. src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/MutationOutcome.cs declares exactly four members, in the order None, Success, NotFound, OutOfRange, with no member carrying an explicit '= n'. This is contract C1 and it is the design the user ruled for at Gate 1, following MASTER-073's ObjectKind.None precedent; a 1-based renumbering with no None member is NOT an acceptable alternative, because it satisfies neither branch of the Microsoft enum guideline. NOT satisfied at the base tree, where the file declares three members with Success first.

A2. The file src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Domain/Entities/MutationOutcomeZeroValueTests.cs exists at exactly that path and contains at least one [Fact]. Stated as its own criterion because a task that only ADDS a file shows an empty 'git diff' to its reviewer; the reviewer confirms this one by listing the path, not by reading a diff.
A3. A test in src/DungeonMaster.Tests/ asserts that default(MutationOutcome) equals MutationOutcome.None. NOT satisfied at the base tree, where default(MutationOutcome) is MutationOutcome.Success.

A4. A test in src/DungeonMaster.Tests/ asserts that (int)MutationOutcome.Success is 1, (int)MutationOutcome.NotFound is 2, and (int)MutationOutcome.OutOfRange is 3 — one observation, that the three pre-existing members kept their relative declaration order. NOT satisfied at the base tree, where (int)MutationOutcome.Success is 0.

A5. A test in src/DungeonMaster.Tests/ asserts that Enum.IsDefined(MutationOutcome.None) is true, recording as an executable fact the reason the guard in A6 must reject a specific member rather than test for definedness. NOT satisfied at the base tree, where MutationOutcome.None does not exist. This mirrors ObjectKindGuardTests.NoneIsADefinedMember_WhichIsWhyTheGuardNeedsItsOwnNoneCondition, written by 6b-viii for the same mechanism.

A6. A [Fact] in src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Common/Handlers/MutationOutcomeExtensionsTests.cs asserts that calling ToResult on default(MutationOutcome) throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException whose ParamName is "outcome" AND whose ActualValue is MutationOutcome.None. Both members are required by contract C3: an assertion on the exception type alone cannot distinguish this guard from a rejection raised one level below it, which is the failure mode recorded against a previous session. NOT satisfied at the base tree, where that call returns Result.Success().

A7. The existing [Fact] ToResult_WithUnrecognisedOutcome_Throws asserts, in addition to the exception type it already asserts, that ParamName is "outcome" and that ActualValue is (MutationOutcome)99. NOT satisfied at the base tree, where the assertion is a bare Should().Throw<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>(). This strengthening is what lets injection B in A9 discriminate.

A8. INJECTION A, run and reverted. In MutationOutcomeExtensions.ToResult, and changing nothing else, make MutationOutcome.None map to Result.Success() while leaving the rejection of undefined values intact. Running 'dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj' under that single change fails the A6 test and leaves ToResult_WithUnrecognisedOutcome_Throws GREEN as a named positive control in the same run. Covering fact reddened: ToResult rejects the zero member. The injection is reverted and the final file satisfies A1 and A6.

A9. INJECTION B, run and reverted, and separate from injection A because a single removal of the whole guard would prove only that SOMETHING was load-bearing. In MutationOutcomeExtensions.ToResult, and changing nothing else, make every value outside Success, NotFound and OutOfRange map to Result.Success() EXCEPT MutationOutcome.None, which keeps its rejection. Running the same command under that single change fails ToResult_WithUnrecognisedOutcome_Throws and leaves the A6 test GREEN as a named positive control in the same run. Covering fact reddened: ToResult rejects a value outside the declared members. The injection is reverted.

A10. The XML <exception> documentation on both ToResult overloads no longer states that the exception is thrown when the outcome is "not a recognised MutationOutcome member", and states instead a condition that is true of MutationOutcome.None, which IS a recognised member. NOT satisfied at the base tree, where both overloads carry the superseded wording.

A11. PRESERVED BEHAVIOUR, deliberately satisfied at the base tree and asserted so that a regression is visible: the existing parameterised test that maps every consequential MutationOutcome member to its expected success flag and ErrorCategory passes with its [InlineData] rows unchanged, so Success still maps to Result.Success(), NotFound to ErrorCategory.NotFound, and OutOfRange to ErrorCategory.Validation.

A12. Every file this task creates or modifies under src/ carries CRLF line endings on every line, verified by counting 0x0D 0x0A pairs in BINARY and comparing that count against the file's line count. This encodes an environment constraint, not a style preference: .editorconfig:64 sets IDE0055 to warning, Directory.Build.props:5 sets TreatWarningsAsErrors=true and :16 sets EnforceCodeStyleInBuild=true, so an LF file fails the build with roughly thirty 'Fix formatting' errors at odd columns that never mention line endings. Three instruments LIE about this in this environment and none of them may be used as the evidence: 'git show <rev>:<path> > file' and 'perl -pe' strip CR; 'sed -n Np file | cat -A' shows no ^M even on a genuine CRLF file; 'grep -c $'\r$'' returns a confident 0 on a correct file. The harness's standing instruction to edit via Bash 'sed' conflicts directly with this criterion — use the Edit tool for every .cs change in this task.

A13. PRESERVED BEHAVIOUR: 'dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.Domain/DungeonMaster.Domain.csproj', the same for src/DungeonMaster.Application, and the same for src/DungeonMaster.Tests each report '0 Warning(s)' and '0 Error(s)'. Satisfied at the base tree by design; asserted because A12's failure mode surfaces here and nowhere else.

A14. PRESERVED BEHAVIOUR: 'dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj' reports 0 failed. The passing COUNT is deliberately not asserted: this task shares the DungeonMaster.Tests project with T2, so any total is a measurement of both tasks and not of this one.

tasks.title: DrawSessionResult gains None at zero, in App.Core only
acceptance: B1. The DrawSessionResult declaration in src/DungeonMaster.App.Core/Map/MapDrawingSession.cs declares exactly four members, in the order None, Added, Closed, Ignored, with no member carrying an explicit '= n'. This is contract C2. NOT satisfied at the base tree, where the enum declares three members with Added first.

B2. The file src/DungeonMaster.Tests/AppCore/Map/DrawSessionResultZeroValueTests.cs exists at exactly that path and contains at least one [Fact]. Stated separately because an added-only file is invisible to 'git diff'; the reviewer confirms it by listing the path.

B3. A test in src/DungeonMaster.Tests/ asserts that default(DrawSessionResult) equals DrawSessionResult.None. NOT satisfied at the base tree, where default(DrawSessionResult) is DrawSessionResult.Added, so a leaked default currently reads at DungeonDetailPage.xaml.cs:1473 as 'a vertex was added'.

B4. A test in src/DungeonMaster.Tests/ asserts that (int)DrawSessionResult.Added is 1, (int)Closed is 2, and (int)Ignored is 3 — one observation, that the three pre-existing members kept their relative declaration order. NOT satisfied at the base tree, where (int)Added is 0.

B5. A [Fact] in src/DungeonMaster.Tests/ drives MapDrawingSession.PlaceVertex through all three of its outcomes on one session — a first vertex, a repeat of the last vertex, and a closing vertex after three or more vertices — and asserts that each returned value is not DrawSessionResult.None. This pins contract C2's requirement that the producer never emits the zero member. NOT satisfied at the base tree, where the assertion does not compile because DrawSessionResult.None does not exist.

B6. INJECTION C, run and reverted. In MapDrawingSession.PlaceVertex, and changing nothing else, replace the 'return DrawSessionResult.Added' at the method's final return with 'return default'. Running 'dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj' under that single change fails the B5 test, and the pre-existing MapDrawingSessionTests assertions on the Ignored and Closed outcomes stay GREEN as named positive controls in the same run. Covering fact reddened: the Added path returns an explicit member rather than the CLR default. The injection is reverted.

B7. INJECTION D, run and reverted, and separate from injections C and E so that each of PlaceVertex's three return paths carries its own covering fact. In MapDrawingSession.PlaceVertex, and changing nothing else, replace 'return DrawSessionResult.Ignored' with 'return default'. Running the same command under that single change fails the B5 test AND the pre-existing MapDrawingSessionTests assertion on the Ignored outcome, while the Added and Closed assertions stay GREEN as named positive controls. Covering fact reddened: the Ignored path returns an explicit member rather than the CLR default. The injection is reverted.

B8. SCOPE BOUNDARY, and deliberately satisfied at the base tree: no file under src/DungeonMaster.App/ is created or modified by this task, and the two equality comparisons at src/DungeonMaster.App/Views/DungeonDetailPage/DungeonDetailPage.xaml.cs:1473 and :1489 are byte-for-byte unchanged. This is the criterion, not a convenience: leaving them unchanged is what makes a leaked DrawSessionResult.None take NEITHER branch and commit no vertex, which is the entire behavioural effect this task buys. It also keeps the task off the Windows TFM, where a running DungeonMaster.App produces MSB3026/MSB3027.

B9. Every file this task creates or modifies under src/ carries CRLF line endings on every line, verified by counting 0x0D 0x0A pairs in BINARY against the file's line count. Same environment constraint and same forbidden instruments as T1's A12 — 'git show > file', 'perl -pe', 'sed | cat -A' and 'grep -c $'\r$'' each return a confident wrong answer here. The harness's standing instruction to edit via Bash 'sed' conflicts with this criterion; use the Edit tool for every .cs change.

B10. PRESERVED BEHAVIOUR: 'dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.App.Core/DungeonMaster.App.Core.csproj' and 'dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj' each report '0 Warning(s)' and '0 Error(s)'. Satisfied at the base tree by design; asserted because B9's failure mode surfaces here and nowhere else.
B11. PRESERVED BEHAVIOUR: 'dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj' reports 0 failed. The passing COUNT is deliberately not asserted: the project is shared with T1.

B12. INJECTION E, run and reverted, and separate from injections C and D so that the third of PlaceVertex's three return paths carries its own covering fact. In MapDrawingSession.PlaceVertex, and changing nothing else, replace 'return DrawSessionResult.Closed' at MapDrawingSession.cs:70 with 'return default'. Running 'dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj' under that single change fails the B5 test AND the pre-existing MapDrawingSessionTests assertion on the Closed outcome, while the pre-existing assertions on the Added and Ignored outcomes stay GREEN as named positive controls in the same run. Covering fact reddened: the Closed path returns an explicit member rather than the CLR default. The injection is reverted. Added at Gate 2 by the user's decision, because B7 as drafted asserted a universal over three return paths while specifying only two injections.

tasks.title: File the enum zero-value triage in the audit record
acceptance: C1. docs/audit/01-domain-application.md contains a new '### CORE-034' entry for MutationOutcome, carrying a YAML block with the same keys and in the same order as the existing '### CORE-017' block (id, layer, severity, category, authority, citation, locations, effort, risk, independent), with authority 'microsoft' and citation https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/design-guidelines/enum. CORE-034 is the next free id: 'grep -ohE "CORE-[0-9]{3}" docs/audit/*.md | grep -oE "[0-9]{3}" | sort -n | uniq | tail -1' returns 033 at the base tree. NOT satisfied at the base tree, where no CORE-034 exists.

C2. The CORE-034 entry states, as the defect, that default(MutationOutcome) was MutationOutcome.Success and that the '_ =>' arm of MutationOutcomeExtensions.ToResult could not catch it because the CLR default IS a recognised member and was mapped straight to Result.Success(). It must state that this differs from MASTER-073, where the zero value was ABSORBED by a '_ =>' arm rather than passed through by one. NOT satisfied at the base tree.

C3. docs/audit/01-domain-application.md contains a new '### CORE-035' entry recording the full triage, which names all FOURTEEN concrete-at-zero production enums, each with its zero member and its class. The fourteen, counted from measurement.md section 3, are: MutationOutcome (Success, A), DrawSessionResult (Added, A), RotationDirection (Clockwise, B), ScaleDirection (Up, B), PathSegmentKind (Line, B), SnapAnchor (Center, C - reclassified from B by C6, which carries the evidence), MapTool (Draw, C), DrawState (Idle, C), NotebookKind (Dungeon, C), NotebookPane (Description, C), CanvasCursorShape (Arrow, C), BehaviorCursorShape (Hand, C), FloorListBandKind (FloorCard, C), ErrorCategory (Validation, C). The entry must give the denominator as 17 production enums, not 16. NOT satisfied at the base tree, where none of the fourteen is filed anywhere.

C4. The CORE-035 entry states the PathSegmentKind blocker in full and with its evidence: AreaConfiguration.cs:16 builds options as new JsonSerializerOptions(JsonSerializerDefaults.General); 'grep -rn "JsonStringEnumConverter\|JsonConverter" --include=*.cs src/' returns zero hits; System.Text.Json therefore writes the ORDINAL into the Areas.Outline TEXT column; and PathSegmentJsonRoundTripTests.cs:26-28 pins "Kind": 0 as Line and "Kind": 1 as CubicBezier. It must conclude that inserting a zero member there is a data migration on persisted rows, not a renumbering, and is out of scope for this session. NOT satisfied at the base tree.

C5. The CORE-035 entry records, for RotationDirection and ScaleDirection, that adding a zero member does not on its own make a leaked default detectable, because both consumers are boolean comparisons — 'dir == RotationDirection.Clockwise' at DungeonDetailPage.xaml.cs:140 and :151, and 'var down = dir == ScaleDirection.Down;' at :167 — whose else-branch would absorb the new member and still perform the operation in the opposite direction. NOT satisfied at the base tree.

C6. The CORE-035 entry reclassifies SnapAnchor from class B to class C and gives the reason from repository evidence: ObjectKindInfo.GetDefaultAnchor (src/DungeonMaster.App/Assets/ObjectAssets/ObjectKindInfo.cs:24-28) returns SnapAnchor.Center as its terminal fallback, so Center is the most-common-default and the enum sits inside the guideline's second branch. NOT satisfied at the base tree.

C7. The CORE-035 entry marks class C as judgment about intent supported by usage rather than as a measurement, EXCEPT for ErrorCategory, for which it cites the measured evidence that the field is stored as ErrorCategory? at Result.cs:31 and ResultOfT.cs:39 so absence is already modelled by null. It must also record that CA1008 does not fire at this solution's AnalysisMode=Recommended, measured by build probe in session 6b-viii, so no analyzer will flag any enum this triage leaves unchanged. NOT satisfied at the base tree.

C8. docs/audit/03-app-shell-and-views.md contains a new '### UI-037' entry for DrawSessionResult, in the same block shape as the entries already in that file, recording both what T2 changed and the follow-up T2 deliberately did not take: the two equality sites at DungeonDetailPage.xaml.cs:1473 and :1489 still carry no explicit rejection of the zero member. UI-037 is the next free id: 'grep -ohE "UI-[0-9]{3}" docs/audit/*.md | grep -oE "[0-9]{3}" | sort -n | uniq | tail -1' returns 036 at the base tree. NOT satisfied at the base tree.

C9. docs/audit/00-master-index.md gains exactly three new rows, numbered 177, 178 and 179 in both the '#' column and the 'MASTER-###' column, for CORE-034, CORE-035 and UI-037 in that order, each row carrying the same column count as the rows above it. 176 is the highest existing row and the row count is also 176 at the base tree, measured by 'grep -cE "^\| [0-9]+ \| MASTER-" docs/audit/00-master-index.md' and 'grep -ohE "MASTER-[0-9]{3}" docs/audit/*.md | grep -oE "[0-9]{3}" | sort -n | uniq | tail -1'. NOT satisfied at the base tree.

C10. Each of the three new index rows has a status cell that contains NO commit hash and does not claim 'done'. A task cannot invoke git, so any hash it wrote would be invented; the closing annotation with its hash is the orchestrator's post-merge docs commit, which is how every prior closure in this file was written (see commit d3b4cbd, 'docs(audit): close MASTER-073 and MASTER-074'). Falsifiable by inspection: the three cells contain no 7-or-40-character hexadecimal token.

C11. The existing '### CORE-017' entry in docs/audit/01-domain-application.md gains an amendment recording that its 6b-viii amendment's reasoning — that renumbering is free because no ordinal is persisted — is specific to ObjectKind, which maps with .HasConversion<string>(), and does NOT generalise: PathSegmentKind persists its ordinal through the Areas.Outline JSON column. The text of the existing 6b-viii amendment is not deleted or rewritten; the new text is added beside it. NOT satisfied at the base tree.

C12. This task modifies only files that are already tracked, and creates none, so its whole change is visible in 'git diff' to its reviewer with no added-file blind spot. Deliberately satisfied at the base tree as a scope boundary: no file outside docs/audit/ is touched, and no file under src/ is touched.

C13. Every count and every universal this task writes into docs/audit/ names the command or the artifact it came from, in the text, at the point of the claim. Specifically: the 14-of-17 figure cites measurement.md; the zero-hits JsonStringEnumConverter claim cites its grep; the CA1008 non-firing claim cites the 6b-viii build probe. This encodes the repository's own standing rule on counts in the audit record, and it is load-bearing here because the figure this session must NOT reproduce — a previous architect's '14 of 16' — is itself an uncited count that survived into a session artifact and had to be corrected by measurement.
